question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should that be Android-specific command work or part of the generic node-advertised tool contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority, private-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and security shape safely.

options.title: Narrow Device Control First
options.body: Accept explicit foreground/permission-gated Android device-control commands and defer ADB and dynamic execution until a stronger execution policy exists.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 and the open candidate PR as the core contract, then let Android expose only approved descriptors through that model.

options.title: Keep high-power execution out of core
options.body: Reject ADB and dynamic Android code execution in OpenClaw core for now and require an external plugin, ClawHub package, or app-specific fork for that authority.

recommendation.title: Narrow Device Control First
recommendation.body: Accept explicit foreground/permission-gated Android device-control commands and defer ADB and dynamic execution until a stronger execution policy exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal for the generic node-to-model tool contract and security boundary is the open candidate PR plus recent node/Gateway/tool history under this account.
